parts.name: Hand
parts.Basic_description: This is the hand of the clock, typically made of metal for rigidity and precision.
parts.Functional_description: It rotates around the clock face to indicate time, driven by the internal clock mechanism.
parts.Movement_description: It moves rotationally around the clock center, controlled by the clock’s motor or gears.

parts.name: Surface
parts.Basic_description: This is the transparent surface of the clock, usually made of glass to protect the hands and dial.
parts.Functional_description: It protects the internal components from dust and damage while allowing visibility of the clock face.
parts.Movement_description: It remains stationary and fixed to the frame.

parts.name: Frame
parts.Basic_description: This is the outer frame of the clock, made of wood, providing structure and aesthetic appeal.
parts.Functional_description: It houses and supports all internal components of the clock, including the mechanism and face.
parts.Movement_description: It is a fixed, non-moving structural component.

parts.name: Button
parts.Basic_description: This is a control button on the clock, made of plastic for easy pressing.
parts.Functional_description: It is used to adjust settings such as time or alarm functions.
parts.Movement_description: It moves linearly inward when pressed and returns to its original position via a spring mechanism.

parts.name: Button
parts.Basic_description: This is another control button on the clock, also made of plastic.
parts.Functional_description: It may serve a secondary function such as setting an alarm or switching modes.
parts.Movement_description: It moves linearly inward when pressed and returns to its original position via a spring mechanism.
